item.title: Minister’s call to graduates
item.description: HEALTH Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu has urged dental graduates still without public-sector placements to approach the ministry directly, as some junior dentists say they have been waiting up to 15 months for employment. “They should just come to HQ and talk with our human resources department,” Dr Lalabalavu told The Fiji Times.
item.content:encoded:
HEALTH Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu has urged dental graduates still without public-sector placements to approach the ministry directly, as some junior dentists say they have been waiting up to 15 months for employment.

“They should just come to HQ and talk with our human resources department,” Dr Lalabalavu told The Fiji Times.

“Or even come up to my office and I can talk with them and see how best we can address their issues.”

The call comes as graduates from the 2023-2024 cohort say they remain unemployed despite completing five-year Bachelor of Dental Surgery degrees, mandatory one-year internships and registration with the Fiji Medical and Dental Council.

“Despite completing all required education and training, many of us have now remained unemployed for approximately 14–15 months since completing our internship,” they said.

The graduates said some had found only inconsistent work in private practices while waiting for public-sector positions.

The 2024 cohort, which completed internships in March 2026, is also awaiting placements after sitting Dental Officer interviews that month. The vacancies were first advertised in December 2025.

The situation has also affected National Toppers Scheme recipients, who are bonded to serve Fiji for seven and a half years but say some have completed only one year of service.

Fiji Dental Association president Dr Parikshath Naidu said the association was aware of graduates struggling to find work but did not have official unemployment figures.

“We have assisted where we could by supporting their registration, sharing advice and looking for job vacancies,” he said.

The association said workforce planning should prioritise basic dental care and employment for local graduates before expanding specialist services.

item.title: Ratu Eparama remembered for lifelong service
item.description: THE late Tui Vuda Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia has been remembered as a dedicated soldier, chief and community leader who served his people and Fiji with distinction. Speaking at his funeral, Captain Savenaca Degei said Ratu Eparama answered the call by the late Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna to young Fijian men to join the military, despite his elders wanting him to remain in Vuda and look after the land.
item.content:encoded:
THE late Tui Vuda Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia has been remembered as a dedicated soldier, chief and community leader who served his people and Fiji with distinction.

Speaking at his funeral, Captain Savenaca Degei said Ratu Eparama answered the call by the late Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna to young Fijian men to join the military, despite his elders wanting him to remain in Vuda and look after the land.

Ratu Eparama joined the Republic of the Fiji Military Forces in 1951 and was deployed to the Malaya Campaign with the First Battalion Fiji Infantry Regiment aboard the Asturias on January 8, 1952.

“He was not merely a soldier by title, he was a soldier by character, discipline, resilient and committed to the task entrusted to him,” Capt Degei said.

Speaking for the Vanua of Vuda, Taukei Nakelo Ratu Josaia Natakele said the late chief remained steadfast in his leadership throughout his life.

“He was 95 but he was still planting sugar cane,” he said.

“He had businesses, he was committed to the work of the church and led and inspired our people.”

Tui Nawaka Ratu Joeli Bulu Derenalagi said Ba would remember Ratu Eparama as a voice of calm during difficult times.

The eighth chief installed through Vuda’s traditional chiefly succession, Ratu Eparama’s tenure included developments such as a new two-storey, eight-classroom building at Vuda District School and efforts towards relocating the military camp to Kubunasarava.

His passing marks the end of an era for the Vanua o Vuda.

item.title: Vuda prepares to name new chief
item.description: THE ninth Tui Vuda will be decided at Viseisei village in Vuda today. The title was left vacant by the late Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia who was laid to rest by the Vanua of Vuda yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
THE ninth Tui Vuda will be decided at Viseisei village in Vuda today.

The title was left vacant by the late Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia who was laid to rest by the Vanua of Vuda yesterday.

The final rights were accorded by the Yavusa Tububere led by Taukei Sawaieke Iliesa Cebaivalu Namuira.

Mr Namuira said while the people of Vuda had been preparing for the final rights for the late Tui Vuda yesterday, they were also looking forward to today when their chief is appointed by the kingmakers or Sauturaga, Yavusa Nakelo.

“It is a new chapter for the Vanua of Vuda,” he said.

“It is not an easy take and one that it is a very important decision to make.

“Because it means a new path, a new chapter and a new leadership for the Vanua of Vuda.

“But that is all in the hands of the Taukei Nakelo and his people to decide.

“So we all look towards their decision and to this new beginning.”

item.title: Crash victim awaits justice
item.description: A FORMER Labasa market wheelbarrow worker, Apenisa Mainaucakoko, is still waiting for justice more than a decade after he was seriously injured in a taxi accident. Mr Mainaucakoko, of Natuvu in Cakaudrove, said the accident happened at night near the Labasa mill in 2016 while he was walking in search of a taxi.
item.content:encoded:
A FORMER Labasa market wheelbarrow worker, Apenisa Mainaucakoko, is still waiting for justice more than a decade after he was seriously injured in a taxi accident.

Mr Mainaucakoko, of Natuvu in Cakaudrove, said the accident happened at night near the Labasa mill in 2016 while he was walking in search of a taxi.

“I tried waving at the taxi to stop, however, it didn’t,” he said.

“That was when I was hit and sustained my injuries.”

In a video uploaded on Facebook, he said the taxi stopped a short distance ahead, and a police vehicle on patrol arrived at the scene at the same time.

He said he was admitted to the Labasa Hospital for about a month because of the severity of his injuries.

“I suffered injuries to my hand, chest and face and was kept under observation by the doctors and nurses.”

Before the accident, he worked as a wheelbarrow worker at the Labasa market, earning a living by transporting customers’ goods. He said the injuries prevented him from returning to the work that had supported him for many years. He said he hoped his case would finally be heard so he could move on with his life.

Questions sent to police more than two weeks ago for comments on the concerns raised by the man remained unanswered when this edition went to press.

item.title: Address causes – Archbishop warns against ‘Band-Aid’ approach to drugs
item.description: THE Government should explore every avenue to address the social factors that push people to use drugs before considering a “needle-syringe program”. Head of the Catholic Church and chairman of the Pacific Council of Churches Archbishop Peter Loy Chong said this while describing the proposed program as a “Band-Aid solution”.
item.content:encoded:
THE Government should explore every avenue to address the social factors that push people to use drugs before considering a “needle-syringe program”.

Head of the Catholic Church and chairman of the Pacific Council of Churches Archbishop Peter Loy Chong said this while describing the proposed program as a “Band-Aid solution”.

He argued that the focus should instead be placed on the factors that drive people to drug use.

“The needle is not the real problem,” he said. “The real problem is people taking drugs, and the whole question — why people take drugs.”

Speaking to this newspaper, Archbishop Loy Chong said there were a variety of reasons why people, particularly adolescents and young people, begin using drugs.

He also pointed to what he described as the “limitedness” and “finiteness” of human beings as another factor that could contribute to drug use.

He said people did not always have the “fullness of life” they desired and could turn to drugs as a means of escaping pain, struggles, and feelings of guilt.

“Because drugs promise them that high. That high that takes them out of the pain, the struggles, the inner struggles of the human person.”

Archbishop Loy Chong said addressing drug use, HIV and the issue of needles required looking at how the issues were connected.

He said the Catholic Church had developed a handbook on responding to drugs, while stressing the need to examine the reasons behind drug use.

“We have to go from HIV, to the needle, the needle to the drugs.

“Drugs, and you have to find out why is it people are taking drugs.”

item.title: Faith fuels Temalesi’s mission
item.description: WHILE many young women her age are focused on enjoying their youth, 23-year-old Hibiscus contestant Temalesi Vakalawa Alutakua has chosen a different path — one centred on faith, teaching and community service. item.content:encoded:
WHILE many young women her age are focused on enjoying their youth, 23-year-old Hibiscus contestant Temalesi Vakalawa Alutakua has chosen a different path — one centred on faith, teaching and community service.

With paternal roots in Kwaio, Malaita, Solomon Islands, and maternal ties to Lamiti, Gau, Ms Alutakua is a scripture teacher at CMFI College and Primary, where she works to nurture young people in faith, values and character.

She also serves in the ministry department at World Harvest Centre, taking part in youth outreach and weekly feeding programs for street-connected children and underprivileged families around Suva.

“It’s not just about the food, it’s about showing them love, sitting with them, praying with them, and reminding them they are not forgotten.”

Ms Alutakua said she entered the Miss Hibiscus contest not for fame, but to use the platform to encourage young people to recognise their worth and God-given purpose.

Her own journey has also taught her the power of forgiveness. She said learning to forgive was one of life’s hardest lessons.

“I’ve always tried to teach myself all the things that I’ve learned throughout were not to hold resentment. If God can forgive me, who am I not to forgive? That is a lesson I’ve learned in life.”

item.title: Police HQ to relocate
item.description: The Fiji Police Headquarters will soon be relocated from Centrepoint in Nasinu to the old Parliament complex in Veiuto, Suva. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe confirmed the move yesterday, saying the Government had approved the relocation.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Police Headquarters will soon be relocated from Centrepoint in Nasinu to the old Parliament complex in Veiuto, Suva.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe confirmed the move yesterday, saying the Government had approved the relocation.

“The Government, through the Prime Minister, has given to police the approval of shifting the police HQ,” he said.

He said funding previously provided by the Australian government through the Australian Federal Police for the construction of a new police headquarters would instead be used to renovate the old Parliament complex.

“So, the fund that was given by Australia to build a new one will be used to renovate,” he said.

The development comes after AFP Commissioner Reece Kershaw met Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua earlier this year to discuss police support, AI capabilities and the development of the new headquarters.

item.title: Biman denies charges
item.description: FORMER deputy prime minister Professor Biman Prasad’s lawyer has urged the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption to avoid any further surprises when the matter returns for trial on September 1. Lawyer Richard Naidu made the comment before Magistrate Yogesh Prasad after the court granted FICAC leave to amend the charges against Prof Prasad.
item.content:encoded:
FORMER deputy prime minister Professor Biman Prasad’s lawyer has urged the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption to avoid any further surprises when the matter returns for trial on September 1.

Lawyer Richard Naidu made the comment before Magistrate Yogesh Prasad after the court granted FICAC leave to amend the charges against Prof Prasad.

Prof Prasad entered a not-guilty plea to the amended charges of a count of failure to comply with statutory disclosure requirements and providing false information in a statutory declaration.

FICAC alleges that between December 30, 2015, and January 31, 2016, being an officeholder of the National Federation Party, Prof Prasad failed to comply with Section 24(1B)(d) by providing to the Office of the Registrar his declaration of assets, liabilities and income as at December 31, 2015, without disclosing his directorship in Platinum Hotels & Resorts PTE Ltd thereby committing an offence contrary to Section 24(5) of the said act.

He is also alleged to have recklessly provided false information in a statutory declaration submitted to the Registrar of Political Parties Act 2013 by solemnly declaring that the particulars contained in his declaration of assets, liabilities and income as of December 31, 2015, were true and complete when the declaration omitted his directorship in Platinum Hotels & Resorts PTE Ltd.

Mr Naidu sought to have the trial commence today, August 13, but Magistrate Prasad maintained his earlier ruling, stating that the defence required adequate time to prepare.
